docs.title: Parameterized SQL queries in Python
docs.text: Never build SQL by string concatenation. Use driver-level parameter binding so the driver escapes values, never structure.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# vulnerable: cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{email}'")
# safe (DB-API drivers):
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = %s", (email,))
# safe (sqlite3):
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?", (email,))

docs.text: Jinja2 autoescaping plus explicit |e for dynamic HTML; never mark untrusted content as safe.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# Flask: keep autoescaping on for .html/.xml templates (default) return render_template("profile.html", username=user_input) # in the template, escaping is automatic: #

{{ username }}

docs.title: Safe file paths in Python
docs.text: Resolve the untrusted path and verify it stays inside the intended root before touching the filesystem.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# vulnerable:
path = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, user_filename)
data = open(path).read()
# safe:
from pathlib import Path
base = Path(BASE_DIR).resolve()
target = (base / user_filename).resolve()
if not target.is_relative_to(base):
    raise HTTPError(400, "invalid path")
data = target.read_bytes()

docs.title: Environment-based secrets in Python
docs.text: Read secrets from the environment or a secret manager at runtime; keep them out of source and history.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# vulnerable:
API_KEY = "sk-live-1234567890"
# safe:
import os
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache
def get_api_key():
    key = os.environ.get("API_KEY")
    if not key:
        raise RuntimeError("API_KEY not configured")
    return key
# plus: rotate any key that ever shipped in a commit (gitleaks --history)

docs.title: Safe subprocess calls in Python
docs.text: Never pass user input to a shell; use argument arrays with shell=False and validate values against an allow-list.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# vulnerable:
os.system(f"ping -c 4 {host}")
subprocess.run(f"convert {src} {dst}", shell=True)
# safe:
import subprocess
if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
    raise ValueError("host not allowed")
result = subprocess.run(
    ["ping", "-c", "4", host],
    shell=False, capture_output=True, timeout=10,
)

docs.text: Allow-list destinations and block private or link-local addresses after DNS resolution; never follow redirects blindly.

docs.title: Safe deserialization in Python
docs.text: Use JSON for untrusted data; never pickle or yaml.load input from users; safe loaders for the rest.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# vulnerable:
import pickle, yaml
obj = pickle.loads(user_bytes)          # arbitrary code execution
data = yaml.load(user_text, Loader=yaml.Loader)
# safe:
import json
data = json.loads(user_text)
import yaml
data = yaml.safe_load(user_text)
# if you must use pickle, sign the payload first and verify before loads.

docs.title: Modern password hashing and crypto in Python
docs.text: Hash passwords with a memory-hard algorithm and per-password salt; avoid MD5/SHA-1 for security purposes.

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
# vulnerable:
import hashlib
hashed = hashlib.md5(password.encode())
# safe (argon2id preferred):
from argon2 import PasswordHasher
ph = PasswordHasher(time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536, parallelism=4)
hash_ = ph.hash(password)
# verify:
ph.verify(hash_, password)
# for general hashing use hashlib.sha256/bcrypt; for tokens use secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
